subject: VAT treatment for multi-rate invoice lines and reverse-charge validation
messages:
From: Elena Costa <accounts@aurora-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-25T09:12:00Z
Subject: VAT handling for multi-rate subscription (EU)

Hi Kimberly,

Quick question from our finance team as we're reviewing next month's charge: Aurora is EU-headquartered (DE) and we have a German VAT ID. Our upcoming invoice will contain two distinct lines: (1) SaaS subscription (monthly licenses) and (2) a one-off integration service performed remotely. For the subscription line we'd expect reverse-charge (B2B) treatment if Redwood validates our VAT ID. For the integration service we believe German VAT (19%) should apply.

Can you confirm Redwood's preferred approach for:
- validating our VAT ID as evidence for reverse-charge
- how you prefer the invoice to show split lines and tax calculations (we need the invoice for our input to claims)
- timeline to reissue or correct the invoice before the 10/01 payment due date

I've attached an example of last month's invoice so you see the current layout (example_aurora_invoice.pdf).

Thanks,
Elena Costa
Accounts Payable
Aurora Retail

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Cc: 
Date: 2026-09-25T11:04:00Z
Subject: Fwd: VAT handling for multi-rate subscription (EU)

Ben / Rafael — forwarding Aurora's question. Attach: proposed-invoice-line-split.xlsx (draft showing subscription at 0% RC and professional services at 19% DE VAT).

Initial triage:
- We can apply reverse-charge on the subscription lines if we validate their VAT ID via VIES and retain the confirmation for our records.
- Professional services performed (even if remote) may be subject to local VAT depending on place-of-supply; Germany will generally tax B2B services carried out in DE at 19% unless covered by RC rules.
- Action needed: request Aurora's VAT certificate & company registration (prefer PDF). Once we validate, we should:
  1) reissue invoice with separate tax lines (subscription = 0% RC, reference to Article/RC note; services = 19% VAT)
  2) include a short VAT note on the invoice that names the buyer VAT ID and VIES validation date
  3) keep an audit copy of the VIES response and the customer's certificate in the transaction record

Rafael — can finance confirm if we need to route the service line through Redwood's EU entity (we currently invoice from US entity for subscriptions) or if we should collect VAT & remit? I'll attach the draft spreadsheet.

Kim

From: Elena Costa <accounts@aurora-retail.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-25T14:30:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT handling for multi-rate subscription (EU)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the quick response. Attached: aurora_vat_certificate.pdf (company registration + VAT certificate). Our VAT ID is DE123456789. We confirm:
- Subscription is a B2B digital supply — we expect reverse-charge (no VAT charged on that line).
- Integration work was contracted as a one-off professional service; the work was performed remotely but the customer is located in DE and our accounting treats that as taxable at 19% (they prefer to have VAT on that line).

We'd prefer Redwood to:
- Reissue the invoice splitting the two lines and showing 0% on the subscription with a note "reverse charge — buyer liable (VAT ID DE123456789)";
- Charge 19% VAT on the integration service line and break out net/VAT/gross;
- Send amended invoice PDF by 2026-09-28 so we can process before 10/01 due date.

Happy to sign any amendment if needed.

Best,
Elena
Accounts Payable, Aurora Retail

From: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-26T08:45:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT handling for multi-rate subscription (EU)

Kim / Ben — finance review summary:
- Confirmed: if customer provides a valid EU VAT ID and we capture and store VIES validation, we can apply the reverse-charge on subscription lines (0% on the invoice). We must retain the VIES response as proof for audit.
- Professional services: treat as taxable in Germany @ 19%. Since Redwood's invoice will come from the US entity in our current flow, we have two options:
  a) Redwood invoiced from EU branch (we have a DE billing entity available under a managed arrangement) — invoice from DE entity and remit VAT through that entity; or
  b) Redwood invoiced from US entity and we collect VAT via our EU fiscal representative / agent (requires additional bookkeeping and a short SOW amendment).

Recommended, lowest-friction approach for this deal: route the one-off service line through our DE managed billing entity and reissue the invoice. That keeps VAT collection and remittance straightforward.

Next steps I propose:
- Kimberly to confirm to the customer we will reissue an amended invoice (split lines), invoice from the DE billing entity for the service line, and include the RC note on subscription lines.
- Ask customer to sign a brief amendment (DocuSign) that confirms acceptance of split billing and new tax treatment.
- Finance will validate VIES and attach validation screenshot to the transaction record.

I've attached the billing-change-playbook.pdf with the checklist for reissuing split invoices and routing to DE entity.

Rafael
Head of Finance Ops

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: Elena Costa <accounts@aurora-retail.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.com, rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: 2026-09-26T09:10:00Z
Subject: Re: VAT handling for multi-rate subscription (EU)

Hi Elena — thanks for the VAT certificate. Plan below and timeline:

Planned changes:
- Subscription (monthly license): reissue with tax = 0% and invoice note: "Reverse charge — buyer liable. Buyer VAT ID: DE123456789. VIES check completed 2026-09-26."
- Integration service (one-off): invoiced from our DE billing entity, VAT applied at 19% (line shows net / VAT / gross).

Action items (for clarity):
1) Aurora: confirm acceptance of split billing and that signing a short amendment is OK (we'll send DocuSign).
2) Redwood: finance will perform VIES validation and attach validation screenshot to the transaction. Rafael will coordinate the DE-entity invoice issuance.
3) Redwood: we will send the amended invoice PDF and a copy of the signed amendment to accounts@aurora-retail.com by end of day 2026-09-28.

DocuSign (amendment): https://docusign.example/envelope/ABC123 (please sign ASAP so we can reissue before your payment due date)
VIES check link we will use (for your records): https://ec.europa.eu/taxation_customs/vies/

Attached: reissued-invoice-draft.pdf (contains the split lines and RC note). Please review and confirm if wording is acceptable or if you want a different phrasing on the VAT note.

If all good, we'll proceed and you should receive the final amended invoice + signed amendment copy by 2026-09-28.

Thanks,
Kim
Senior Sales Ops
Redwood Inference
